dominant_strengths: Faithful iOS settings idiom with crisp icon tiles, consistent corner radii and well-balanced grouped sections
Dark palette with restrained accent colors; toggle greens and destructive red sit comfortably without clashing
Clear information hierarchy via uppercase section labels, primary/secondary text pairing, and aligned controls
dominant_weaknesses: Highly derivative of native iOS Settings — distinctiveness and innovation are minimal, no signature voice or invention
Footer meta text 'v4.2.1 · Last saved just now' feels cramped against action buttons, weakening bottom rhythm
Segmented control and dropdown styling differ subtly from row toggles, creating mild control-language inconsistency
fix_priorities: Introduce one signature element (custom control, micro-interaction hint, or layout twist) to escape pure iOS mimicry
Unify control vocabulary: align segmented, dropdown, and toggle visual weights and active-state colors
Rebalance footer: separate version metadata from primary actions or right-align with more breathing room
rationale.norman_balance: Strong behavioral clarity and decent visceral polish, but reflective payoff is low because the design borrows wholesale from a familiar system.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it reads cleanly as an improved settings panel with sensible grouping and controls, though 'improved' over baseline iOS is marginal.
